subject: DI03000081

body.en:
Definition

An electromechanical converter exchanges mechanical and DCelectrical power through magnetic interaction.

Classification / representative type

  • Generator converts shaft input to electrical output;motor converts electrical input to shaft output.Both use substantially the same basic construction.
  • Excitation may be permanent-magnet or wound-field.Wound-field machines include separately excited,self-excited shunt,series and compound types.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Yoke:cast iron in some small machines or steel in larger designs;it supports the poles and provides the magnetic return path.
  2. Pole core and shoe:magnetic steel,commonly laminated where required;the shoe spreads flux across the air gap and supports the field coil.
  3. Field winding:insulated copper turns produce main MMF.Shunt coils use many fine turns;series coils use fewer heavy-current turns.
  4. Armature core:laminated electrical steel with slots carries the conductors and reduces eddy-current loss;thin laminations are insulated from one another.
  5. Armature winding:insulated copper conductors in slots are connected in a prescribed lap/wave pattern to commutator segments;parallel paths affect voltage/current rating.
  6. Commutator:hard-drawn copper segments separated by mica insulation form a rotating mechanical switching device;it is not a continuous slip ring.
  7. Brushes and holders:carbon/graphite brushes with controlled spring pressure make sliding electrical contact;wrong pressure or dirt increases heating and sparking.
  8. Steel shaft,bearings,end covers,fan and terminal box support rotation,cooling and protected connections.Insulation separates conductors from the core and frame.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Field excitation establishes flux from a north pole,across the air gap,through armature iron and back through the south pole/yoke.
  2. In generator operation a prime mover drives the shaft;armature conductors cut the field and acquire induced EMF.
  3. Individual rotating coils have alternating EMF;the commutator changes their brush connections at appropriate rotor positions.
  4. Brushes therefore deliver unidirectional terminal output,with ripple reduced by many coils/segments.
  5. In motor operation supplied armature current interacts with field flux to exert force and develop torque.
  6. Commutator switching reverses the relevant coil current as it moves between poles so net torque retains its direction.
  7. Rotation also induces a counter/back EMFin a motor;the current is limited by voltage balance,not by armature resistance alone once running.

Applications

Industrial drives,exciters,controlled DCgeneration and teaching models;select a type for the actual duty.

Limitations and safety

Brush wear,sparking,losses and maintenance limit use.Powered tests need guarded rated machines and qualified supervision.

Why laminate armature iron?

To limit eddy currents while retaining a magnetic path;lamination does not eliminate hysteresis.

title.en: 1.2 Generator principle,Faraday law and right-hand rule

body.en:
Understand the idea

EMFis generated by a change of flux linkage;energy comes from the prime mover,not from magnets alone.

Explanation and application

  • Faraday:e=−dλ/dt=−Nturn dΦ/dt;the minus sign expresses Lenz opposition.For a straight conductor,e=Blv sinθwhen the geometric assumptions apply.
  • Fleming right hand:thumb motion,index finger field NtoS,middle finger induced conventional current.All are mutually perpendicular.
  • Use the right hand for generation and the left hand for motor force;reverse motion or field to reverse generated polarity.
  • An open-circuit generator can have voltage without load current.Closing a load allows current and produces opposing electromagnetic torque.

Understand the idea

Let P=poles,Φ=webers/pole,Z=total active armature conductors,N=rpm,A=parallel paths.

Explanation and application

  • One conductor cuts PΦwebers during one revolution.Time per revolution=60/Nseconds.
  • Average EMFper conductor=(PΦ)/(60/N)=PΦN/60.
  • Each parallel path contains Z/Aconductors in series.Thus Eg=PΦZN/(60A)volts.
  • Simplex lap:A=P;simplex wave:A=2.Do not substitute number of turns for total conductors without accounting for two active sides per turn.
  • Eg∝ΦNat fixed winding geometry.Φcan saturate,so it is not always proportional to field current.

Given and assumptions

P4,Φ0.02Wb,Z480,N1000rpm;compare simplex windings.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Lap:A4;Eg=(4×0.02×480×1000)/(60×4)=160V.
  2. Wave:A2;Eg=320V.Same conductors/flux/speed,different series conductors per path.

Interpretation and check

This is an ideal calculated comparison,not permission to reconnect an actual armature.

Understand the idea

Identify field connection before using current or voltage equations.

Explanation and application

  • Separately excited:independent field supply;armature current equals load current and external field power must be counted in overall efficiency.
  • Shunt:field across terminal supply;If=V/Rsh,Ia=IL+If.Suitable regulated-purpose DCsupplies need field control,not an assumption of perfectly constant voltage.
  • Series:field in armature/load path,Ia=Ise=IL;voltage varies strongly with current.Specific booster/constant-current duties are historical/specialised uses.
  • Compound combines shunt and series fields.Cumulative fields assist;differential fields oppose.Long-shunt spans armature plus series field;short-shunt spans armature only.
  • Cumulative compound can be under-,flat-or over-compounded;used where terminal-voltage droop must be compensated.Differential compound droops sharply and is unsuitable as a general constant-voltage supply.

body.en:

Explanation and application

Acharacteristic is a relation at declared speed/field conditions;do not compare unrelated operating points.

Explanation and application

  • Magnetic/OCC:Egversus Ifat constant speed and open armature output.Residual voltage starts the curve;the knee marks saturation.
  • Internal characteristic:generated EMFunder load versus load/armature current,with the chosen current clearly labelled.Armature reaction can reduce generated EMF.
  • External characteristic:terminal Vversus IL.It includes armature/series resistance,brush drop and excitation changes,so it differs from internal Eg.

h.en: Why internal and terminal curves differ

body.en:
Understand the idea

Separate magnetic-load effects from resistive terminal drops.

Explanation and application

  • Internal Egunder load includes armature-reaction flux changes.The terminal voltage is lower by the applicable armature/series resistance and brush drops.
  • The curves are illustrative;declare the horizontal current definition and speed/field settings when plotting actual measurements.

Understand the idea

Load current creates its own MMFand changes the main-field distribution.

Explanation and application

  • Armature reaction distorts flux,cross-magnetises the main field and can introduce demagnetisation depending on brush position/saturation.Neutral plane may shift.
  • Commutation is current reversal in an armature coil while its commutator segments are shorted by a brush.It must finish within the short commutation interval.
  • Coil inductance produces reactance voltage opposing rapid current reversal;poor commutation causes sparking,heating and segment damage.
  • Interpoles aid local current reversal;compensating windings oppose armature MMFunder pole faces.Correct brush grade/pressure and clean true commutator matter.
  • Never adjust brushes or inspect exposed rotating live parts by hand.Isolate,verify dead and follow manufacturer maintenance instructions.

Understand the idea

Track power through the correct machine direction;generated power is not terminal output.

Explanation and application

  • Generator:mechanical input minus iron/friction/windage loss gives EgIa.Armature copper Ia²Ra,brush drop×Iaand series-field loss are deducted before terminal/field power division.
  • Shunt field loss=VIf=V²/Rsh;series field loss=Ia²Rsewhen its current equals Ia.Copper loss varies approximately as current squared;iron loss depends on flux/frequency/speed.
  • Stray-load losses represent additional load-dependent nonideal effects;not every loss is constant or captured by a single I²Rterm.
  • Generator output=VIL;overall η=useful output/total supplied input.Motor stages reverse the energy conversion,but copper and rotational losses are still positive.
  • Generator regulation%=(VNL−VFL)/VFL×100at the same specified speed and field setting.Negative regulation can occur with over-compounding.
  • For an assumed fixed-loss plus variable copper-loss model,maximum efficiency occurs when variable loss equals the relevant constant loss;state which field/brush losses are included.

Given and assumptions

V220V,IL20A,Rsh110Ω,Ra0.2Ω,total brush drop2V,rotational/iron loss300W.

Step-by-step solution

  1. If=220/110=2A;Ia=22A;Eg=220+22×0.2+2=226.4V.
  2. Output=4400W;field loss440W;armature loss96.8W;brush loss44W.Total loss880.8W.
  3. Mechanical input=5280.8W;EgIa=4980.8W;η=83.3207%.

Interpretation and check

Check:EgIa−armature loss−brush loss=V(Ia)=4840W,which splits into4400Wload+440Wfield.
